text: Se ho tempo, vengo volentieri. | If I have time, I'd love to come.
why: The Italian is se + present with a plain present (vengo), the 'likely' case this lesson teaches; "I'd love to" is the English conditional, the very form the lesson contrasts it with (se avessi tempo, verrei).
fix: If I have time, I'll be happy to come.

text: Me ne dà means "could you give me some" or "could you give me two."
why: Me ne dà alone never means "give me two"; the number comes from a word that isn't quoted (due), so the gloss adds meaning.
fix: Me ne dà? means "could you give me some?", and with a number, me ne dà due? means "could you give me two?" It's what you say at the deli counter when you want more.
